# Official HTTP 2.8.2: pending body cancellation

This directory contains the official `tauri-plugin-http` 2.8.2 crates.io source,
from Tauri's `http-v2.8.2` tag. Original MIT/Apache licenses are retained.
The crates.io archive SHA-256 is
`46f1afc4200ba2e8b596c378d5756d0056febf8755f1563633d98f6bd7fffb2f`.
The application pins version `=2.8.2` and selects this copy using
`[patch.crates-io]`; its main Cargo.lock remains authoritative. No new HTTP
engine or public plugin API is introduced.

## Scope of the patch

The original response resource has an empty `Resource::close`. A pending body
read holds an Arc, so removing the resource-table entry does not release the
response or its live connection. The original read also uses an unsafe mutable
alias of that Arc's contents.

`src/commands.rs` replaces this response resource/read path with a mutex
holding an optional official reqwest response, an atomic closed flag and a
Tokio Notify. A read registers its notification before testing the flag, then
selects the existing reqwest chunk future against cancellation. Resource close
wakes a pending read; cancellation/EOF/error drops the response. The existing
commands, scopes, redirects, request/client behavior, IPC bytes and JS API are
preserved. Concurrent body reads now serialize without unsafe aliasing.

Independent review also found that the official JS client deliberately exposes
a null body for statuses 101, 103, 204, 205 and 304. It never reads/cancels their
native response resource. The private register_response helper now immediately
closes that resource for exactly those statuses while retaining the original
numeric rid field in the public reply. All other status/body behavior is
unchanged. The repeated actual HTTP regression receives 204/205/304 responses
and verifies their returned resource IDs are absent while an unrelated 200 body
remains present and readable. Informational 101/103 membership is tested only
at the predicate level because reqwest handles interim responses separately.

`src/momoki_cancel_tests.rs` starts a real local TCP server, sends one HTTP
chunk, stalls the next chunk, closes the actual Tauri resource-table entry,
then verifies that the read exits with RequestCanceled and the server sees
disconnect. `src/scope.rs` adds only a test proving the product's generated
exact-origin patterns preserve host, scheme, port and IPv6 boundaries.

The unpatched native reproduction was run before this change: the server did
not disconnect within 300 ms after resource close, and disconnected only after
the pending task was aborted. This is native resource/transport evidence;
actual packaged renderer Stop and close/reload still require separate product
acceptance. Renderer pagehide/beforeunload also aborts active HTTP requests
because Tauri's resource-table clear does not call Resource::close.

## Reproduce

From `desktop/tauri`, using the repository's fixed toolchain launcher:

```sh
node scripts/tools.mjs cargo test \
  --manifest-path src-tauri/vendor/tauri-plugin-http/Cargo.toml \
  --offline --no-default-features \
  --features rustls-tls,http2,charset,system-proxy
```

Only the application Cargo.lock is tracked; a library-local lock generated by
the standalone regression command is ignored. Task evidence records original
file hashes/VCS identity, the exact patch, unpatched reproduction and patched
logs. Preserve those records when archiving the task.

The cookie-disabled official crate emits two existing unused-variable warnings
in its optional cookie on-event closure. They are retained upstream bytes;
the application still passes clippy with `-D warnings`. Cookie jars, tracing,
unsafe headers and dangerous client settings remain disabled.
